item.title: BB warns against 22 unauthorized online payment platforms
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank on Sunday issued a public warning notice identifying 22 unlicensed online payment platforms operating in the country and urging the public to refrain from using or participating in their activities.
According to the central bank's Payment Systems Supervision Department, providing payment services or operating a payment system without a valid license from Bangladesh Bank violates Section 4(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024, and is punishable under Section 37(1) of the same act.
The department identified the following 22 platforms providing payment aggregator services without statutory approval: BohudurPay, ZiniPay, PayTiller, BengaliPay, Payora BD, SohojPay BD, EasyPayWay, AK Pay, BD PAY, ShajgarPay, AsthaPay/CPay, UddoktaPay, Walletmix, BttPay, Easy Pay Automation, UniquePay BD, BD AUTO PAY, RH Pay BD, EzePay, AutoPay Ltd, Biswasto, and PipraPay.
The central bank advised all individuals, institutions, and businesses to refrain from conducting transactions with or engaging in the operations of these unlicensed payment aggregators to avoid legal penalties and financial risks.
Regulatory actions leading up to this notice have targeted unauthorized digital apps and platforms involved in high-interest online micro-lending, illegal gambling, and financial fraud.
The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) and Bangladesh Bank routinely instruct commercial banks and mobile financial services (MFS) to suspend transaction channels for unauthorized platforms that bypass central bank supervision, endanger consumer data, or engage in predatory lending practices.
In July 2024, the Parliament passed the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024, significantly strengthening Bangladesh Bank's statutory authority to oversee non-bank digital financial services.
Under Section 4(2) and Section 15(2) of the Act, operating any payment platform, digital wallet, or online transaction gateway without explicit authorization from Bangladesh Bank is illegal.
The law introduced strict penalties under Section 37(1), declaring unlicensed financial operations a cognizable, non-bailable offense punishable by imprisonment, steep fines, or both.
Certain platforms listed in the notice had previously faced regulatory action. For instance, Bangladesh Bank officially canceled the Payment System Operator (PSO) license of Walletmix Limited in November 2023 after detecting unauthorized and illegal financial transactions that violated regulatory terms.
Despite losing its license, platforms attempting to operate or offer payment aggregator tools without authorization remain subject to enforcement.
The Payment Systems Supervision Department launched these sweeps to mitigate systemic risks in the digital ecosystem.
Unregistered payment aggregators and gateways often lack mandatory Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism (AML/CFT) safeguards, exposing consumers and merchants to risk of financial loss, delayed settlements, data breaches, and illegal fund diversion.

item.title: JCI Dhaka Sparks convenes 3rd general members' meeting 2026
item.description:
JCI Dhaka Sparks convened its 3rd General Members' Meeting (GMM) of 2026 on September 26 at the Sirajul Alam Khan Centre and Research Institute in Dhaka.
Local President Raihan Ahmed Dip chaired the assembly, which gathered over 75% of the board of directors alongside national leaders and visiting chapter presidents.
A primary highlight of the meeting was the official launch of the "Green Village" climate initiative.
Presented by director Sahaduzzaman Shrabon, the project aims to tackle deforestation and biomass loss in the Chittagong Division by replacing traditional firewood cookstoves with IoT-enabled eCook Induction Stoves from clean-tech partner ATEC.
Real-time carbon reduction data from the stoves will be verified under Gold Standard accreditation standards.
Local President Raihan Ahmed Dip announced a national Memorandum of Understanding with Hajj with Ayesha, granting all active JCI Bangladesh members a minimum 10% discount on administrative and service fees, as well as special package and ticket privileges.
Earlier, the chapter co-organized a training session on JCI Discover and JCI Explore alongside JCI Dhaka Astral and JCI Dhaka Young.
Conducted by NEVP Shahmina Isha Mannan, the session saw over 40 young leaders complete their core modules.
Six new members were inducted into the chapter: Mir Sadman Ali, Dr. Nazmun Nahar Hafsa, Fatema Tuz Zannat Bristy, Md. Samiul Haque, Tasnuva Rahman Nishim (Opshori), and Abrar Farhan Zaman.
Exceptional performance was recognized with Member of the Month crests presented to ASM Mosabbir Tanim (July), Tasnuva Rahman Nishim (August), and Moumita Siddika (September).
Special recognition was also given to past local president senator Noor E Alam Bhuiyan.
Activity and treasury reports were adopted, covering past projects such as Fight the Bite and PASC 2026.
Members were encouraged to prepare for upcoming events, including the 2026 TOYP Banquet at Radisson Blu Water Garden Hotel on October 17 and the 2026 JCI World Congress in Clark, Philippines, from November 11–15.

item.title: NRB Bank, MetLife renew partnership for 8th consecutive year
item.description:
NRB Bank PLC has renewed its partnership with MetLife Bangladesh for the eighth consecutive year to provide enhanced insurance protection benefits for eligible credit cardholders.
Under the agreement, the bank's eligible credit cardholders will receive insurance coverage designed to help settle the outstanding balance on their credit cards in the event of death or permanent disability, subject to policy terms and conditions.
Eligible cardholders will also be entitled to an In-Hospital Cash Benefit for each hospitalization, helping them manage medical expenses during treatment and recovery.
Tareq Reaz Khan, managing director & CEO of NRB Bank PLC, and Ala Ahmad, chief executive officer of MetLife Bangladesh, has signed the agreement on behalf of their respective organizations.
Tareq Reaz Khan, managing director & CEO of NRB Bank PLC, said: "Our customers expect banking services that add meaningful value to their everyday lives. Our partnership with MetLife Bangladesh for the eighth year will allow eligible credit cardholders to continue benefiting from insurance protection designed to support them and their families during difficult and unexpected situations."
Ala Ahmad, chief executive officer of MetLife Bangladesh, said: "Financial protection can make an important difference during an unexpected health crisis or other unforeseen event. By continuing our partnership with NRB Bank PLC, we aim to provide impactful insurance benefits that can help reduce financial worries and support greater peace of mind."
NRB Bank is one of the leading providers of card issuance and digital financial services in Bangladesh.
The bank serves customers through multiple channels, including digital banking, branch banking, agent banking, and internet banking, and offers a diversified range of modern, technology-driven banking products and services to meet customers' evolving needs.
MetLife Bangladesh, which has been operating in the country since 1952, currently serves more than one million individual customers and over 900 corporate clients.
The company continues to maintain its leadership position among life insurers in Bangladesh in claims settlement, paying Tk2,853 crore in claims in 2025 and Tk1,384 crore during the first six months of 2026, the highest claims payouts in the industry for the respective periods.
MetLife Bangladesh also maintained a claims settlement ratio of 98% in 2025, one of the highest in the industry.
Senior officials from NRB Bank PLC and MetLife Bangladesh attended the signing ceremony.

item.title: UCB’s ARFL wins ‘Project of the Year’ award for digital innovation
item.description:
United Commercial Bank PLC (UCB) has achieved a significant milestone in its digital transformation journey as its Agri Rural Fast Loan (ARFL) initiative has been named Champion Project of the Year, Information Technology (Medium Category) at the Bangladesh Project Management Symposium & Awards 2026.
The event was recently organized by the Project Management Institute (PMI), Bangladesh Chapter, at a hotel in the capital.
State Minister of Planning Md Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki attended the event as chief guest.
Deputy managing director & chief operating officer of UCB Md Abdullah Al Mamoon was present at the event along with other senior officials of the bank.
ARFL represents UCB’s commitment to making financing faster, simpler and more accessible through technology.
The initiative is designed to facilitate agricultural loan disbursement to eligible farmers within a single day.
The recognition of ARFL represents an important milestone in UCB’s broader digital transformation journey and showcases the capabilities of UCB ONE- UCB’s Core digital banking platform and technology foundation for delivering integrated, scalable and customer-centric financial services.
Commenting on the recognition, UCB highlighted the award as a proud milestone for the bank specially an agriculture and rural entrepreneurship initiative and an affirmation of its ongoing efforts to harness digital innovation for more efficient and inclusive financial services.

item.title: Shahe Alam stresses ensuring solar power use in govt offices, institutions
item.description:
State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development, and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, MP, on Sunday urged the relevant departments and agencies to work in a coordinated manner to ensure the use of solar power in government offices and institutions quickly.
“The relevant departments and agencies should advance their work according to their respective action plans and regularly review the progress of implementation,” he said, mentioning that the activities to use solar power must be implemented quickly.
He made the call at a meeting held in the conference room of the Rural Development and Cooperatives Division at the Secretariat, said a PID release.
He also said he would soon inspect the activities on the ground to install solar power at various institutions.
At the meeting, the ongoing activities and implementation progress of action plans of the concerned departments and agencies were reviewed to increase the use of solar power in government offices and institutions.
Various aspects of reducing electricity costs of government institutions and expanding the use of renewable energy through increased use of solar power were also discussed.
The meeting stressed taking necessary initiatives to implement action plans for using solar power at field-level offices of respective agencies as well as offices and institutions located in Dhaka.
Rural Development and Cooperatives Division Secretary Dr Rafiqul Mohamad chaired the meeting.
Managing Director of Small Farmers Development Foundation Mohammad Mahbubur Rahman, Director General of Bangladesh Academy for Rural Development; Comilla Saif Uddin Ahmed, Registrar and Director General of the Department of Cooperatives; Md Selim Fakir, Director General of Bangladesh Rural Development Board; AKM Tarek; and heads of various departments and agencies under the ministry were present at the meeting.
Heads of various departments and agencies located outside Dhaka also joined the meeting online and presented the activities and progress of their respective institutions.

item.title: Singapore wants to provide border security assistance to Bangladesh
item.description:
Outgoing Singaporean Chargé d’Affaires has expressed his country’s interest in providing modern technology and technical assistance to strengthen Bangladesh’s border and immigration security.
Outgoing Chargé d’Affaires of Singapore Mitchel Lee said this during a courtesy call on Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed at his Home Ministry office in the Bangladesh Secretariat on Sunday, a PID handout said.
During the meeting, they discussed the issues of bilateral relations, capacity building of the Bangladesh Police, modernization of security systems at airports and land ports, technology transfer, economic and trade cooperation, and other issues of mutual interest.
Lee highlighted Singapore’s willingness to support Bangladesh in adopting modern technology for border and immigration security, as well as providing technical assistance in these areas.
He said bilateral relations and trade between Bangladesh and Singapore were continuing to expand.
Ahmed also expressed hope that the appointment of a full-fledged Singaporean high commissioner to Bangladesh would be completed soon to further strengthen bilateral trade and relations.
Ahmed emphasized on the longstanding diplomatic and economic ties between the two countries.
He said Bangladesh government is working to establish modern, technology-based immigration and border security systems in the frontier and airports.
The minister also expressed hope that cooperation between the two countries would expand through joint efforts to combat extremism, police training and transfer of technologies.
Singapore’s incoming Chargé d’Affaires Philip Ong, Additional Secretary of the Political and Immigration Wing of the Home Ministry Dr Ziauddin Ahmed, and Second Secretary of the Singapore mission Dhanya Lingesh were present.

item.title: Riaz Hamidullah: Dhaka-Delhi ties 'organic', conversation must continue
item.description:
Outgoing Bangladesh High Commissioner to India M Riaz Hamidullah has described the relationship between Bangladesh and India as “organic” and rooted in mutual interdependence and shared interests.
“Very simple - this is a relationship which, on several occasions, I've said is organic ... of mutual interdependence. It's a relationship which is in shared interests,” he said.
Hamidullah, who assumed charge as Bangladesh High Commissioner to India on April 7, 2025, is set to leave New Delhi early next month to take up his new assignment as Permanent Representative of Bangladesh to the United Nations in Geneva, a senior official said.
The diplomat said differences in views, perspectives and approaches are natural in any close relationship particularly between two countries that share an intimate geography.
“But with those, we must remain engaged; carry on conversation, as we need to unpack the interaction between people far more than it is today,” he told Indian media ANI in an interview.
He said people-to-people engagement should go beyond conventional exchanges, noting that broader interaction could reach millions of people and help strengthen understanding between the two countries.
“That’s an unattended space that remains,” he said, referring to the need for greater engagement at the people-to-people level.
While communication between ministries and governments remains important, Hamidullah said he sees a much larger space that can be addressed through broader social and educational engagement.
“For example, among students, school-going children and universities,” the envoy said, adding that greater engagement in these areas could reach “millions” of people and make a “distinct difference” to the relationship between the two countries.
Reflecting on his recent experiences in India, Hamidullah, in a post on his verified X account, spoke about a visit during which an interaction with students at Delhi Public School (DPS) Srinagar left a lasting impression on him.
He visited the school after arriving in Srinagar on September 3, saying he was particularly struck by its inclusive and scholastic environment and the energy of its more than 5,000 students.
DPS Srinagar was founded in 2003 by Vijay K Dhar under the D P Dhar Memorial Trust. The Dhar family has longstanding links with Bangladesh, including through the late D P Dhar, who played a significant role in the formation and early years of Bangladesh.
Hamidullah said his interaction with students at the school offered him a different perspective on how young people view issues such as borders and identity.
A Class XII student, RJ Fatima, introduced herself to him as a radio jockey and invited him to the school's digital radio station, which, he said, has been operating since 2019.
“She just asked me and got me into her radio studio, and we got into conversation,” Hamidullah recalled. What surprised him most, he said, was Fatima’s question: “How do you look at borders?”
“Imagine, sitting in Srinagar, a girl asking this,” he said, adding that he took the question in “absolute candour” and responded to her openly.
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi recently called for keeping trade, cultural exchanges and people-to-people connectivity between Bangladesh and India moving forward, saying such issues should not be held back by political developments.
Talking to reporters after a cultural program in Dhaka earlier this month, he said the two countries would continue discussing various issues, but matters such as the Maitree Express, the Ganges Water Treaty, trade and cultural exchanges should not be allowed to get stuck.
“These are the things of ordinary people,” said the High Commissioner, highlighting the importance of keeping people at the center.
The High Commissioner said trade restrictions on both sides have to be eased. Otherwise, he noted, people will suffer.
He said there is no need to rush and the political process will take its own course. But the work that concerns ordinary people must continue, Trivedi said.
India on Tuesday reiterated that it wants to take its relationship with Bangladesh forward in a positive, constructive and forward-looking manner and expressed its willingness to discuss all bilateral issues between the two countries.
“India desires a positive, constructive, and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh,” Indian Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said while responding to a question about bilateral ties during a media briefing in New Delhi.
Jaiswal said India is ready to discuss all bilateral issues with Bangladesh through the existing structured mechanisms.
“Our intent is to take this relationship forward in a positive direction, in a constructive direction, in a forward-looking manner,” he said.
A vibrant ‘Ilish Fest’ celebrating Bangladesh’s national fish, Ilish, was held at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi on Saturday.
The event, held at the “Maitri” Auditorium of the High Commission, brought together prominent Indian politicians, diplomats, civil society representatives, academics, journalists and cultural personalities.
During the festival, prominent Indian personalities unveiled the book A Fish Called Ilish, published in Dhaka.
The event centred on Ilish, which is deeply rooted in Bengali heritage, culture and culinary traditions. It also provided an opportunity to showcase Bangladesh’s rich cultural heritage and hospitality, with guests enjoying a variety of Ilish dishes alongside traditional Bangladeshi cuisine.
The guests appreciated not only the distinct taste of Bangladeshi Ilish but also the emotions, traditions and cultural values associated with the fish.
Former Indian Minister of State for External Affairs and noted journalist M J Akbar, former diplomat and politician Mani Shankar Aiyar, human rights activist and social thinker Syeda Hameed, former Indian ambassador Ronen Sen, eminent sociologist Ashis Nandy and other distinguished personalities attended the program.
The guests praised the taste of Bangladeshi Ilish and the overall organization of the festival.
The event also highlighted Bangladesh’s heritage, culture and hospitality, while guests expressed hope that such initiatives would contribute to further strengthening the friendly ties between the peoples of Bangladesh and India.
Speaking after the book launch, Bangladesh High Commissioner Riaz Hamidullah said Ilish is closely linked to Bangladesh’s identity and the fish is deeply intertwined with the country’s social and economic fabric.
The High Commissioner also noted that Bangladesh has five Ilish sanctuaries and that the government has taken various initiatives to increase Ilish breeding and production. These efforts have contributed to increased conservation and production of Ilish, he said.

item.title: BB governor: Int’l agreements being signed to identify, freeze laundered assets
item.description:
Initiatives have been taken to amend the "Distressed Asset Management Act" and the "Money Loan Court Act" to allow for judicial settlement within six months in order to curb defaulted loans and money laundering, announced Bangladesh Bank governor Md Mostaqur Rahman.
He stated that agreements are being made at the international level to identify and freeze assets laundered out of the country.
Additionally, 11 special joint investigation teams have been formed on the initiative of Bangladesh Bank.
He made these remarks as the chief guest at an exchange-of-views meeting titled "Implementation of Incentive Packages Announced by Bangladesh Bank for Private Sector Development" held at Bangladesh Agricultural University (BAU) on Saturday (September 26).
The event was organized at the university's Syed Nazrul Islam Conference Hall under the initiative of Bangladesh Bank to raise public awareness and inform stakeholders about the package.
Regarding the recovery of the country's fragile economy, Mostaqur Rahman noted that except for foreign exchange reserves, almost all economic indicators were in a risky and negative state when he assumed office.
Multiple special plans have been undertaken for economic recovery and bringing back laundered money. At the same time, effective measures are being taken to address irregularities and looting in the banking sector.
Regarding the distribution of low-interest funds, he stated that idle bank deposits are being utilized to provide funds at 4% interest.
These funds will be distributed to the SME and agriculture sectors at interest rates between 7% and 8%.
Furthermore, the process of launching a new fund to create young entrepreneurs is underway.
Plans include offering entrepreneurs a 50% grant and loans at interest rates of 4% to 5%.
Beneficiaries will be selected through a completely transparent process involving successful private sector entrepreneurs.
In the first session of the event, attendees were briefed on the incentive package announced by Bangladesh Bank, followed by an open Q&A session where bank officials and entrepreneurs from various levels raised their issues and inquiries.
During the meeting, organizers detailed the bank-announced incentive package, stating that this entrepreneur search program will initially be conducted across 64 upazilas from 8 divisions.
Ten individuals will be identified initially from each upazila, totaling 640. Phased over time, a total of 5,000 young entrepreneurs will be brought under this financing scheme.
Based on their needs, entrepreneurs will receive a financing package of up to maximum Tk20 lakh at a profit rate of 4% to 7%, comprising 50% bank loan and 50% grant.
Presided over by Md Arifuzzaman, executive director of Bangladesh Bank's Mymensingh region, special guests included Prof GM Mujibur Rahman, student affairs adviser of the university, and SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar, Mymensingh Divisional Commissioner.
Faculty members from various university departments, senior bank officials, and entrepreneurs from different areas of Mymensingh were also present at the event.

item.title: Tarique returns home after five-day US visit
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman returned home on Sunday morning after wrapping up his five-day visit to the United States to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).
“An Emirates flight carrying the Prime Minister, his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman and members of his entourage reached Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport via Dubai around 8:21am,” PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu told UNB.
After a six-hour transit stop in Dubai, the Emirates flight departed Dubai International Airport for Dhaka at 2:15am local time, Shiplu said.
Tarique arrived in Dubai from New York at 8:23pm local time on Saturday on an Emirates flight after leaving New York on Friday night.
At John F Kennedy International Airport, Tarique and Zubaida were seen off by Bangladesh Ambassador to the United States Tareq Md Ariful Islam, Bangladesh’s Permanent Representative to the UN Irene Khan and senior officials of the UN mission and embassy.
The Prime Minister arrived in New York on September 21 to attend the UNGA and delivered his maiden address as Prime Minister at the General Debate on September 24.
During the five-day visit, he held around 30 bilateral and side meetings with heads of state and government, senior international officials and representatives of international organisations.
He held bilateral meetings with the leaders of Türkiye, Iran, Pakistan, Croatia, Haiti, Bhutan and Thailand, as well as senior officials from Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Sweden.
The meetings focused on bilateral relations, trade and investment, economic cooperation, manpower, the Rohingya crisis and regional and international issues.
The Prime Minister also met UN Secretary-General António Guterres, World Bank President Ajay Banga, UN officials and other international dignitaries.
In his UNGA address, Tarique highlighted Bangladesh’s priorities on global peace and security, climate change, sustainable development, economic cooperation and the Rohingya crisis.
He also outlined the government’s three-R strategy—Recovery, Restoration and Reconstruction—to rebuild Bangladesh.
During the visit, the Prime Minister also attended high-level events on the Rohingya crisis, sea-level rise, climate action and a just transition, and integrating midwifery into primary healthcare.
On the economic front, he attended a breakfast meeting hosted by JPMorgan Chase with Wall Street representatives, where he said Bangladesh is “open for business” and invited global investors to invest in the country.

item.title: Salman Muqtadir’s studio attacked over ‘extortion refusal’; 2 held
item.description:
Content creator and actor Salman Muktadir's studio has allegedly been attacked, extensively vandalized, and looted after he refused to pay extortion money.
Salman alleged that BNP-affiliated individuals had demanded money from him, and the attack occurred after he refused to pay. Two people have been detained in connection with the incident. Muhammad Giyas Uddin, officer-in-charge (OC) of Cantonment Police Station, confirmed this to Dhaka Tribune on Sunday morning.
He said that upon receiving news of the attack, police went to the scene, where two people were detained. He also stated that weapons were recovered. According to those involved, the incident had earlier taken place around 10:30pm on Saturday at New Greenery Properties near ECB Chattar in the capital. An official at the studio claimed that around 150 people suddenly entered the premises at 10:30pm and began vandalizing it. He alleged that several of them were carrying machetes and firearms. Seeing the dangerous situation, the officials present at the studio fled and hid in the toilet. It is alleged that the attackers followed them there as well and, at gunpoint, took their mobile phones and wallets. Various essential equipment kept in the studio was also reportedly taken. Salman Muktadir was not in Dhaka at the time of the incident. Upon hearing the news, he flew back to Dhaka. He later went to the studio, saw the damage, and addressed the matter in a Facebook Live session. Salman said the studio contained footage from various clients' shoots along with necessary equipment and materials for various projects. Because these items were taken, the extent of the damage could be substantial, though he could not immediately specify an exact figure. In the Facebook Live, Salman said that a great deal of client footage and shooting equipment had been kept at the studio, and losing them has caused both financial loss and major work-related problems. Showing the extensive damage to his studio, Salman said: "Our studio has been destroyed."
He claimed that there are very few studios like his in the country dedicated to creative work and arts and culture, and that its destruction represents an overall loss. Alleging that BNP-affiliated people were involved in the attack, Salman said: "You BNP people who did this — this is your extortion. Why are you destroying my dream?" Despite the attack, Salman said he will not stop working. Addressing his staff, he said: "Relax, this is nothing. We'll keep working right here." Salman noted that the studio was not just a business for him — it was tied to the employment and creative work of many young people. So even though the studio was damaged in the attack, he doesn't want to stop. In his words: "I will not stop. I will continue my passion. If not from within the country, then I'll continue it from abroad."

item.title: 9 arrested over vandalism, looting at Mirpur health centre
item.description:
Nine people have been arrested in connection with the looting and demolition of the Radda MCH-FP Centre, a private healthcare facility in Section 1 of Mirpur, Dhaka, police said.
Two truckloads of allegedly looted goods have also been recovered from the site, according to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP).
DMP Deputy Commissioner of Media and Public Relations Akhtar Hossain disclosed the information in a statement on Sunday morning.
He said police were identifying and arresting those involved in the attack and looting while continuing operations to recover the stolen goods.
Efforts are also underway to arrest the remaining suspects and recover the rest of the looted items, the statement said.
According to Radda, the Radda MCH-FP Centre has provided free primary healthcare, maternity and family planning services to underprivileged women and children for 50 years in partnership with the government.
Late Thursday night, heavy machinery was allegedly used to demolish the entire facility, including one permanent building and three semi-permanent buildings.
The attackers allegedly left after putting up a signboard for “Samomona Do22 Association Limited” at the front of the property.
Radda officials said a large quantity of vaccines and office equipment was looted during the attack.
Radda Executive Director Nasrin Akhtar filed a case with Shah Ali police station over the incident. The case names local BNP leader Hanif and 200-250 others as accused.
According to the case statement, a group of people entered the premises after scaling the boundary wall, carrying hammers, sticks and homemade weapons.
They allegedly beat and tied up night guards Andrio Sarkar and Abdul Hai before using an excavator to demolish several structures, including a family planning centre and the quarters of the clinic in-charge, doctor and deputy clinic in-charge.
The complaint also alleges that furniture and equipment were vandalized, while doors and windows of the ultrasound, vaccination and laboratory rooms were smashed.
The attackers allegedly took medicines and medical supplies, an ultrasound machine, generator, computers, a printer, refrigerator, air conditioner and steel cabinets.
After allegedly threatening the night guards, the attackers put up a cooperative society banner and signboard at the site, according to the complaint.
Four people arrested on Friday in connection with the incident were sent to jail by a court on Saturday.
They are Md Sohel, 22; Md Juwel, 23; Md Jihad Hasan, 21; and Md Rabbi, 20.
They were arrested during separate operations conducted on Friday night, police said.

Acting on a tip-off, a DNC team raided a cottage named Tuberose inside the lake area of Pubail Resort Club on Friday and recovered the narcotics, he said.
The arrested individuals are Mohammad Moniruzzaman Tanjim, 29; Tushar Ahmed Nishu, 32; Mahidul Islam Rahat, 28; and Kashfia Nishat, 25.
The seized items include 21 MDMA tablets, also known as ecstasy; 24 grams of kush ; 1 gram of cocaine; four bottles of foreign liquor; 20 grams of strawberry-dream-infused gummies; a digital video recorder; three iPhones; and an Oppo phone.
Based on information obtained during interrogation, Md Emdadul Islam Mithun said Tanjim, Nishu and Rahat organised the event and operated the resort under the banner of “Sonic Plus.”
He said various types of synthetic narcotics were allegedly supplied to young men and women attending the event.
According to information provided by the resort authorities, Tanjim, Nishu and Rahat had rented the club to organise the event, the DNC official said.

item.title: Bangladesh, Turkiye discuss PM's participation in COP31
item.description:
Bangladesh and Turkiye have discussed the possible participation of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in COP31, to be hosted by Turkiye in Antalya.
The discussion took place when State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir met Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Friday on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, according to a Foreign Ministry press release.
During the meeting, they exchanged views on the upcoming climate summit, including the prime minister's possible participation. However, the press release did not mention any decision on this.
The two sides also discussed high-level visits, defence cooperation, renewable and green energy and investment opportunities for Turkish companies in Bangladesh.
Kobir invited Turkiye to participate in an international sports conference that Bangladesh plans to host in early 2027.
Both sides expressed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

item.title: LGRD minister urges students to focus on studies for brighter future
item.description:
Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan on Saturday urged students to remain focused on their studies and attend classes regularly, saying proper education is essential for building a strong foundation for the future.
"You must prepare yourselves for the future through education. There is no room for negligence when it comes to studies. Students must attend classes and I urge teachers to ensure that no classes are missed," he said.
The minister made the remarks while addressing a program as the chief guest at the Teacher-Student Centre (TSC) of Dhaka University (DU), stressing the need to maintain a balance between academic pursuits and other activities.
"Of course, you will engage in politics, social policy and economics, but not at the expense of your education," he said. Highlighting the importance of quality higher education, Moyeen Khan said academic excellence plays a vital role in establishing a country's strength and leadership globally.
"We often talk about the United States as the world's leading nation. Many believe it is because of its wealth or advanced fighter jets, tanks and weapons. I disagree," he said.
"In my view, the United States is a leading nation because, under any recognised standard, 70 to 80 of the world's top 100 universities are American. That academic excellence has helped elevate the country to the top," he added.
Recalling the rich academic heritage of Dhaka University, the minister urged all concerned to uphold the prestige and reputation of the country's premier institution of higher education.
"The tutorial system at Dhaka University was modelled after Oxford University. If we do not preserve the reputation of this prestigious and traditional institution -- if students wander around without studying, classes are not held, and teachers and students remain absent -- how will we move this nation forward?" he questioned.

Police member’s mother, wife killed in Purbachal road crash
item.description:
A police member’s mother and wife were killed after a truck hit them while they were crossing a road in Dhaka’s Purbachal 300-ft area around 10pm on Friday.
The truck fled the scene after the incident, and police are working to identify it. The deceased were Afroza Akter Shanta, 28, and the mother of police member Mehedi Hasan.
Mehedi Hasan said his mother and wife were crossing the road together when the truck hit them. They were rescued and taken to the emergency department of Kurmitola General Hospital, where doctors declared his mother dead.
Afroza, who was critically injured, was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) for advanced treatment. She died while undergoing treatment at around 3:30am on Saturday.
Mehedi said their home is in the Sridhara area under Kadamtoli police station in Dhaka. His father, Azizul Haque, is a sub-inspector (SI) at Dhaka City Special Branch.
Inspector Habibur Rahman, in-charge of the DMCH police camp, said, quoting doctors, that another woman had died at Kurmitola General Hospital in the incident. He said Afroza Akter Shanta was later taken to DMCH, where she died while undergoing treatment, and her body was handed over to the family without an autopsy.
Sohrab Hossain, officer-in-charge of Khilkhet police station, said police went to the scene after receiving the news but found no vehicle there.
He said: “CCTV footage from the scene is being collected to identify the truck involved.”
A case filed by the police regarding the incident is currently under process.

Radda healthcare vandalized case: Four arrested sent to jail
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Saturday sent four people arrested over the attack, vandalism and looting at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur to jail.
Shah Ali police station Sub-Inspector Md Atowar Rahman, also the case investigating officer, produced the accused before the court and sought an order to keep them in jail.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Siddique Azad granted the application and ordered that the four be sent to jail.
The accused are Md Sohel, 22, Md Jewel, 23, Md Jihad Hasan, 21, and Md Rabbi, 20.
Sub-Inspector Lutfur Rahman of the prosecution department confirmed the matter and said no bail application was filed on behalf of the accused.
According to the investigating officer's application, the 4 accused admitted involvement in the incident during questioning. Information was also obtained from them about their participation in the attack in exchange for money.
However, they are not residents of the Shah Ali police station area, so their names and addresses could not be verified immediately.
The application further said the accused could obstruct the investigation if released on bail and there was a possibility of them going into hiding. It therefore sought to keep them in jail until completion of the investigation.

item.title: Commerce minister: Sylhet-Dhaka six-lane highway to be fully ready by mid-2029
item.description:
The Sylhet-Dhaka highway will be fully ready for traffic after being upgraded to six lanes by mid-2029, Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir said on Saturday.
He also announced plans to establish an artificial intelligence (AI) training centre in Sylhet to help young people develop skills for the information technology sector.
The minister made the remarks as the chief guest at the inauguration ceremony of the Metropolitan Business Association at a convention hall in Sylhet city.
He said work on upgrading the Sylhet-Dhaka highway to six lanes is progressing as part of ongoing initiatives to improve the country's communication network.
Once implemented, the project will improve connectivity between Sylhet and other parts of the country and help expand investment and trade, he said.
The minister said he had discussed establishing an AI training centre in Sylhet with the ICT minister and that a final decision would be taken after bringing the minister to Sylhet next week or the following week.
He said the initiative was aimed at equipping young people with skills in the information technology sector.
“Many young people in the country are earning through freelancing. If opportunities are created for young people in Sylhet to join this sector through training, they will be able to work with different organisations at home and abroad,” he said.
Muktadir said improving connectivity, information technology and law and order was essential to increasing investment in Sylhet.
There is no alternative to infrastructure development and creating skilled human resources for the overall development of a region, he said.
On law and order, the minister said the presence of drugs or juvenile gangs in an area negatively affects investment.
He said importance was being given to strengthening technology-based surveillance to ensure security.
The minister also announced an initiative to bring Sylhet city under advanced CCTV surveillance.
He said the cameras would be capable of facial recognition and effective surveillance at night.
Leaders and businessmen of the Metropolitan Business Association attended the program.

item.title: Narayanganj trawler capsize: Three siblings found dead in Meghna River
item.description:
Three members of a family, who sank in the Meghna river after a trawler capsized in Sonargaon upazila of Narayanganj district on Thursday due to inclement weather, were found dead on Saturday.
The deceased were identified as Samina, 17, Sajib, 24 and Samin, 5—three siblings who went missing at the time of the accident with their father Helal Uddin, who remains missing.
The divers from local Fire Service recovered the bodies from in front of Al Mostafa Factory in Boidderbazar area of the upazila between 2:55am and 8:10am, said Abdullah Al Arefin, deputy director of Narayanganj Fire Service.
“Search operations are underway to rescue the remaining missing person,” he said.
Mohammad Zahed Chowdhury, station master of Sonargaon Fire Service and Civil Defence Station, said the trawler sank at around 1:30pm on Thursday.
On information, the diver conducted a rescue operation around 4:50pm and continued until 3am.
The operation resumed at 7am on the following day, he said.
Underwater cameras were used in the search, while divers also conducted searches using various methods, he added.
Shah Kamal, inspector and in-charge of the Boidderbazar Naval Police Outpost, said the trawler carrying 14 passengers with two cows and a goat from Homna upazila in Cumilla district sank in the Meghna River during storm on Thursday.
All of them were returning from the wedding of Sajia Akter and Shishir in Haria area in Boidderbazar of Sonargaon upazila.
Later, a woman identified as Rashida was found dead during the trawler capsize while four people including Helal and his three children remained missing.
